clue.text: Like lightning strike: power cuts

indicators.note: something that cuts into a word sits inside it, splitting it in two

parts.note: a raid is a sudden attack or strike
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: A lightning-fast strike in which electricity supplies are cut off.
explanation.walkthrough: The colon divides definition from wordplay; power goes into the middle of the strike, after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Lightning is proverbially fast, so 'like lightning' is a simile for very quick.

clue.text: More costly dental procedure to cover cap of tooth: measure for changing plates

indicators.note: covering something means going around it, so the first word encloses the letter

parts.note: richer, as in a richer diet, can mean more expensive

indicators.note: a cap sits on top, so in a down answer it is the first letter

parts.note: the first letter of tooth
a dentist scales teeth to remove tartar

explanation.surface: A pricey dental job capping a tooth and fixing dental plates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plates' suggests dentures, but it means tectonic plates moving in an earthquake.
explanation.definitionFit: The Richter scale rates earthquake magnitude, and earthquakes happen when tectonic plates shift.

clue.text: They introduce prince and Epstein, originally during walks

parts.note: P abbreviates prince

indicators.note: during means in the middle of, so the letter sits inside the walks

parts.note: rambles are leisurely walks

indicators.note: originally means at the origin, so only the initial letter is used

parts.note: the first letter of the surname

explanation.surface: A topical jibe about Prince Andrew walking with Jeffrey Epstein.
explanation.walkthrough: The E goes in after the first letter of the walks.
explanation.definitionFit: Preambles are introductory statements that come before the main text.

clue.text: Liverpool fan upset? Not after their match with Everton?

indicators.note: upset means turned upside down, which in a down entry flips the word's order

parts.note: Liverpool FC play in red and their fans are the Reds
by a time means not after it

explanation.surface: A Liverpool supporter left upset after the game against Everton.
explanation.walkthrough: Liverpool and Everton are the two big Liverpool city clubs, so their meeting is the Merseyside derby; the question mark marks a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: A derby is a match between local rivals, and Liverpool versus Everton is a famous example.

clue.text: Brilliant person standing to perform

parts.note: standing in the sense of social rank or class
to act is to perform on stage

explanation.surface: A star performer gets a standing ovation.
explanation.definitionFit: A class act is an informal idiom for someone outstandingly talented or impressive.

clue.text: Cuddles lots after stripping bare

indicators.note: stripping takes the outer layer off, so the first and last letters go

parts.note: scant means bare or barely sufficient
oodles means lots

explanation.surface: Lots of cuddling after getting naked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stripping bare' reads as undressing, but stripping acts on the word for bare, removing its outside letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To canoodle is to kiss and cuddle amorously, so the third-person verb matches cuddles.

clue.text: Cuts lines on graphs

definitions.meaning: first meaning: gets rid of, as with jobs or budgets
second meaning: the reference lines of a chart

explanation.surface: Budget cuts plotted as lines on graphs.
explanation.walkthrough: The two meanings are different words spelt alike: the verb to axe, and the plural of axis.
explanation.definitionFit: Axes is both the verb form 'axes' meaning cuts and the plural of axis, the reference lines of a graph.

clue.text: Food put out past eight

indicators.note: something put out is disturbed or displaced, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Dinner was served after eight o'clock.
explanation.definitionFit: Spaghetti is long thin pasta, a staple Italian food.

clue.text: Man acquiring ecstasy that's easily obtained

indicators.note: acquiring means taking something in, so the man holds the extra letter

parts.note: a chap is a man
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A man buys ecstasy that is readily available.
explanation.definitionFit: Something cheap costs little, so it is readily got without much outlay.

clue.text: Deals in these clubs: Chelsea missing Abramovich, ultimately in arrangement with Arsenal

definitions.note: a descriptive definition: bargains are found at these events

indicators.note: an arrangement puts things in a new order, so the letters are reordered
missing means a letter is absent, so one is taken away from the club name

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games
taken as written

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter of the name is taken

parts.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the former Chelsea owner's surname
taken as written

explanation.surface: Football transfer dealing between Chelsea and Arsenal after Roman Abramovich's departure from Stamford Bridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deals' and 'clubs' suggest transfer business, but clubs is just the card-suit letter. Chelsea loses its H before being mixed with Arsenal.
explanation.definitionFit: Clearance sales are shop events selling off stock cheaply, so bargain deals are found at them.

clue.text: Three schools needing repair to get drier

indicators.note: something needing repair is broken, so the letters must be rebuilt in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Three dilapidated schools need repairs to become drier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drier' reads as an adjective about damp buildings, but it is the noun for something that dries.
explanation.definitionFit: A clothes horse is a folding frame on which laundry is hung to dry indoors.

clue.text: Nonsense to members? Conservative backtracking

parts.note: taken as written
M stands for member, doubled for the plural

indicators.note: backtracking means going back the way you came, so the word is read from right to left

parts.note: a Tory is a member of Britain's Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A sneer at a Conservative policy U-turn put to party members.
explanation.walkthrough: Tory is the everyday name for a British Conservative.
explanation.definitionFit: Tommyrot is a dated British colloquial word for foolish talk or rubbish.

clue.text: Check mirror: learner driver in place to practise religiously?

parts.note: CH is the chess notation for check
to ape is to mirror or copy someone
the L-plate marks a learner driver in Britain

explanation.surface: A driving-test instruction: check your mirror, learner, somewhere you can practise devotedly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Check mirror' reads as a driving lesson, but each word is a separate piece; 'practise religiously' puns on doing something diligently.
explanation.definitionFit: A chapel is a small building or room used for Christian worship, a place where religion is practised.

clue.text: The Lion after game: weak spot in order

parts.note: RU is rugby union
Leo is the zodiac sign of the lion
a flaw is a weakness or defect

explanation.surface: A rugby-tour report: the British and Irish Lions found a weakness after the match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Lion after game' places the zodiac sign after the rugby abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: The rule of law is a society's principle of legal order, where everyone is bound by the same laws.

clue.text: Getting on train that's traditional

parts.note: getting on means ageing
to school someone is to train them

explanation.surface: Boarding a train, the old-fashioned way.
explanation.definitionFit: Old-school describes something done in an established, old-fashioned style.

clue.text: Wife and a new catch make out on return: they dream of a new life

definitions.text: they dream of a new life

parts.note: W abbreviates wife
taken as written
N abbreviates new
to nab is to catch

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to make out something is to see it

explanation.surface: A wife and her new partner kiss on their return from honeymoon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make out' suggests snogging, but it means discern; only that piece is turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Wannabees aspire to be someone else, such as a celebrity, and so dream of a different life.

clue.text: Pull to get sex, specifically?

parts.note: to tow is to pull a vehicle
IT is a coy euphemism for sex

explanation.surface: A cheeky question about whether pulling someone is specifically about getting sex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pull' suggests chatting someone up, British slang for seducing, but here it means haul.
explanation.definitionFit: To wit is a formal phrase meaning namely, that is to say, introducing a precise detail.

clue.text: Opening present and flowers in this?

parts.note: a window is an opening in a wall
a present is something that comes in a box

explanation.surface: Opening a gift of flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a definition by example: flowers are one thing grown in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A window box is a planter fixed to a window sill, where flowers are grown.

clue.text: Checked out patient before doctor's introduction

parts.note: a doctor may call a patient a case

indicators.note: an introduction comes at the start, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter of the word doctor

explanation.surface: A patient is discharged from hospital before the doctor even arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: To case a place is slang for scouting it before a burglary.
explanation.definitionFit: To case somewhere is criminal slang for inspecting it in advance, so checked out is the past tense match.

clue.text: Awareness of time, I must go in

indicators.note: going in means entering, so this letter is placed inside the other word

parts.note: time spent in prison is a sentence
taken as written

explanation.surface: Knowing one's time has come and one must go in, as if to prison or surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doing time' is prison slang, hence a sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: Sentience is the capacity to feel and perceive, a basic form of consciousness.

clue.text: Crazy state of uniform: note frilly edging

indicators.note: an edging runs around the border, so this word goes round the other pieces

parts.note: frilly trimmings are often lacy
U is Uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet
N is the standard abbreviation for note

explanation.surface: A dress-code memo: the uniform must have frilly trim.
explanation.walkthrough: The frilly word goes round the pair, which sit after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Lunacy is madness, a state of being insane; its name comes from the old belief in the moon's influence.

clue.text: Sleep with unoccupied playboy like Terry?

parts.note: a nap is a short sleep

indicators.note: unoccupied means empty, so the inside is removed and only the outer letters stay

parts.note: the outside letters of playboy

explanation.surface: A womaniser named Terry taking a nap.
explanation.walkthrough: Terry looks like a man's name but is terry towelling, a fabric with raised loops.
explanation.definitionFit: Nappy means having a nap, a raised pile, as terry cloth does; terry is also classic nappy material.

clue.text: Weight on American, mostly comfort eating? It goes up and down

indicators.note: something eating another takes it inside itself
mostly means not all of it, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: to soothe is to comfort
A abbreviates American
WT is the abbreviation for weight

explanation.surface: Weight goes on Americans who comfort-eat, and the scales go up and down.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'X on Y' puts X after Y, so weight follows American; comfort loses its last letter and swallows that pair.
explanation.definitionFit: A sawtooth line or wave rises and falls in a jagged zigzag, like the teeth of a saw.

clue.text: He's not entirely honest, supported by Mike Pence?

definitions.text: He's not entirely honest, supported by Mike Pence?

indicators.note: not entirely means falling short of the whole, so the final letter is lost

parts.note: true means honest
the initials of the vice-president

explanation.surface: A jibe at a president of dubious honesty, propped up by his vice-president.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supported by' puts the initials below in a down answer. The whole clue also describes the man.
explanation.definitionFit: Donald Trump was the US president whose vice-president was Mike Pence, and his truthfulness was often questioned.

clue.text: Shoot up, wanting cocaine in arm?

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the drug's letter is removed

parts.note: to shoot up is to rise or climb
C is slang for cocaine

explanation.surface: A drug user, out of cocaine, injecting into a vein in the arm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shoot up' and 'arm' conjure injecting drugs, but shoot up means ascend.
explanation.definitionFit: An arm is one of the body's limbs, so the general word stands for the specific one.

clue.text: Surgical procedure: model figure receiving it for partner?

parts.note: an op is an operation

indicators.note: receiving means taking something in, so the model holds the other piece

parts.note: a model poses for an artist
taken as written
a figure is a number

explanation.surface: A cosmetic surgery to give a model the figure their partner wants.
explanation.definitionFit: Your opposite number is your counterpart, the person holding the equivalent role on the other side.

clue.text: Learning timetable as friend's coming back by coach

indicators.note: coming back means returning, so the word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: an ally is a friend, with the possessive 's
a coach is a long-distance bus

explanation.surface: A school trip: a friend returns on the coach to the timetabled lessons.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe of friend's is ignored, as crosswords allow.
explanation.definitionFit: A syllabus sets out the topics of a course of study, a plan for what is learned when.

clue.text: Mythological creature, Erinyes, primarily, following couple of Greek characters

parts.note: pi and xi are letters of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter counts

parts.note: the first letter of the Greek Furies' name

explanation.surface: The Erinyes, Greek Furies, come after a pair of Greek figures in a myth catalogue.
explanation.walkthrough: Erinyes is a red herring for the definition: they are Greek mythological creatures but only lend a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A pixie is a small mischievous fairy of English folklore, a creature of legend.
